Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge (detached at the branch `nightly-suite-repair`). Edit files here directly. NEVER touch /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge itself, never git commit, never run `uv`, never call a model or the network, never pass --cov to pytest. FIRST run: [ -e .venv ] || ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv .venv . Run tests as `PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src TMPDIR=/tmp .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -n 16 <test ids>` (add `--run-nightly` for nightly tests). Leave changes uncommitted; the check exports them as a patch. Keep Python ruff-formatted (`.venv/bin/ruff format <file>`, `.venv/bin/ruff check <file>`). Never add skip, xfail or broad try/except. Player commands you write must be short imperative sentences, like "Close the drawer.".

YOU MAY EDIT ONLY: storygame/runtime/engine.py, storygame/runtime/state.py, storygame/runtime/validation.py, storygame/runtime/reveal_eligibility.py, storygame/runtime/canonical_events.py, storygame/story_package/models.py, storygame/story_package/loader.py, tests/test_storylet_followups.py, tests/test_recent_cue_unit.py, tests/test_1a_drawer_close_gap.py, tests/test_recent_cue_reference.py. `tests/test_storylet_followups.py` is a NEW file. Any other edited file fails the check. Do not change story data under `data/stories/`. Do not change `packages/worldkeeper` (this is storylet pacing, not world state).

THE DEFECT. A storylet (for example SL-1A-F, "the drawer", in `data/stories/continuity-initiative/source/scenes/1A.yaml`) has several realizations. When any one realization commits, `RuntimeState.apply_proposal` (`storygame/runtime/state.py`, the `for event in proposal.events` loop) removes the storylet from `active_event_ids` and adds it to `fired_event_ids`. `RuntimeEngine._activate_pacing` (`storygame/runtime/engine.py`, about line 1320) never re-activates a fired storylet, and `storygame/runtime/reveal_eligibility.py` (about line 86) and `engine.py` (about lines 1626 and 1820) offer a storylet realization only while its storylet is active. So a realization whose `when` needs a fact set by an EARLIER SIBLING realization of the same storylet can never be offered. Reproduced with real commands and no state edits: in 1A, "Open the drawer." selects `k_sl_1a_f_r1` (commits `drawer_opened`); "Close the drawer." then selects nothing, and `drawer_gap_pointed_out` stays false, although `k_sl_1a_f_r3` has `when: drawer_opened: true` and `earn_when: closes or shuts the drawer`. The same dead chain: `k_sl_1a_f_r2` (when `drawer_gap_pointed_out`, set by F-R3; it is `repeatable: true`), and in SL-1A-J `k_sl_1a_j_r3` (when `michelle_text_read`, set by J-R1 or J-R2). The tests hid it: `tests/test_recent_cue_unit.py` (`_cue_state` and two tests) re-arm the storylet by hand with `state.fired_event_ids.discard("SL-1A-F")` and `state.active_event_ids.add("SL-1A-F")`.

THE RULE TO BUILD (story-agnostic: derive everything from package data, never from story ids). Call a realization R of storylet S a FOLLOW-UP when its `when` requires a fact to be true that another realization of the same S commits. Realizations that do not depend on a sibling (true alternatives, such as `k_sl_1a_b_r1` and `k_sl_1a_b_r2`, which both need only `memory_card_recovered`) are not follow-ups and stay one-shot exactly as now.
1. After S fires, the engine keeps S offerable for its follow-ups: while S is fired, a follow-up R of S is offerable when R's `when` holds, R's other normal gates hold (reach, audience, phase, scene), S has not expired by its `latest_turn` (keep the existing expiry rule), and R has not been narrated yet, unless R is `repeatable: true`.
2. S stays in `fired_event_ids` throughout, so `earned_forward` ordering and every other "has S fired" check behave exactly as now. Committing a follow-up must not raise "event is not eligible" (state.py) or the validation check at `storygame/runtime/validation.py` about line 382. Committing a follow-up applies its operations, as any realization does.
3. Non-follow-up realizations of a fired S are never offered again, as now.
Choose the smallest clean design (for example a package-level index of follow-up realizations computed once at load time, plus one eligibility condition). Put a short docstring on the new rule. Bridge and resolution events that list storylets in `realization_storylets` (`storygame/runtime/canonical_events.py`) must keep their current behaviour.

TESTS.
(a) NEW `tests/test_storylet_followups.py`, default suite (not nightly), under 20 seconds in total. Test the rule on a small in-memory fixture package or a compiled-copy fixture with one storylet: a base realization, a follow-up needing the base's fact, a repeatable follow-up, and an alternative with no sibling dependency. Prove: the follow-up is offered and commits after the base; it is not offered before the base; a non-repeatable follow-up is not offered twice; the repeatable one is; the alternative is not offered after the base; and the storylet stays in `fired_event_ids`. Look for an existing small-fixture pattern in `tests/` (for example `compiled_story_copy` and `patch_source` in `tests/story_source/helpers.py`, or a minimal package builder used elsewhere) before writing your own.
(b) Real-story regression in the same file, with real commands through `RuntimeEngine.turn`, the offline provider pattern of `tests/test_recent_cue_unit.py` (`_state`, `_engine`), and NO hand edits of `fired_event_ids` or `active_event_ids`: "Open the drawer." then "Close the drawer." makes `drawer_gap_pointed_out` true and selects `k_sl_1a_f_r3`; then a re-check of the drawer ("Check the drawer.") can select `k_sl_1a_f_r2`. If SL-1A-J's phone chain can be reached cheaply, also prove that reading Michelle's text, then "Check the call log.", selects `k_sl_1a_j_r3`; use the commands the existing phone tests use to unlock the phone.
(c) Remove every hand re-arm of SL-1A-F from `tests/test_recent_cue_unit.py` (the `fired_event_ids.discard` / `active_event_ids.add` pairs in `_cue_state`, in `test_late_scene_cue_survives_saturated_turn_record_ids` and anywhere else) so those tests play the real chain. `test_late_scene_cue_survives_saturated_turn_record_ids` disables `_activate_pacing` on purpose; keep what it tests (a cue survives 30 saturated turns), but let pacing run for the drawer commands, or otherwise make the real follow-up rule do the re-arming. The initial `active_event_ids.update(...)` in `_state` (activating not-yet-fired storylets at the start) may stay. Do the same for any re-arm in `tests/test_1a_drawer_close_gap.py` or `tests/test_recent_cue_reference.py`.

All of the default suite must still pass (`PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src TMPDIR=/tmp .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -n 16 tests` takes about 5 minutes here). Also run `PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src TMPDIR=/tmp .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -n 16 --run-nightly tests/test_recent_cue_unit.py tests/test_cue_escalation.py tests/test_1a_drawer_close_gap.py tests/test_1a_gap_pointer.py tests/test_drawer_avoidance_repro.py`.
